newsitem.title: USA: Sexual harassment alleged at Hooters restaurant chain.
newsitem.headline: Sexual harassment alleged at Hooters restaurant chain.

text.p: A former waitress, with the backing of the federal Equal Employment Opportunites Commission, said Tuesday she filed a sexual harassment suit against her former employer, the Hooters restaurant chain.

Annette Phillips said she filed a lawsuit against Atlanta-based Hooters America Inc., a chain known more for its scantily clad waitresses than for its cuisine. The suit has the backing of the Washington-based Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law.

Phillips said that working at the Hooters restaurant in Myrtle Beach, S.C., meant putting up with male managers who exposed themselves to women employees and being forced to play degrading sexual games, without the right to seek legal protection against harassment.

The EEOC also filed a motion to enter the case as a "friend of the court" and has filed a 33-page brief supporting Phillips in the suit, which seeks to become a class action on behalf of non-management female employees.
"I am here today on behalf of myself and any other Hooters employees who feel that they have been abused," Phillips, who stopped working at Hooters in June, told a news conference.
A spokesman for Hooters said the company had no immediate response to the lawsuit or to Phillips' allegations.

Attorneys for Phillips said they believed there were more than 1,000 female Hooters employees who could be affected by the suit. Thomas Henderson of the Lawyers' Committee said he was aware that there had been other suits against Hooters for sexual harassment, but said he could not comment further.

Phillips worked as a waitress and bartender at Hooters from May 1989 until June 1996, when she said the atmosphere at the restaurant became more than she could bear. She said she experienced frequent episodes of sexual harassment.
Privately owned Hooters is a $350 million restaurant chain with locations in 38 states, Canada, Puerto Rico and Singapore.
